passages.text: Manasseh was twelve years old when he became king, and he reigned in Jerusalem fifty-five years.
passages.sermon: Manasseh became king when he was twelve years old.\r\nHe ruled in Jerusalem.\r\nHe ruled for fifty-five years.
passages.original: בֶּן־ שְׁתֵּ֥ים עֶשְׂרֵ֛ה שָׁנָ֖ה מְנַשֶּׁ֣ה בְמָלְכ֑וֹ וַחֲמִשִּׁ֤ים וְחָמֵשׁ֙ שָׁנָ֔ה מָלַ֖ךְ בִּירוּשָׁלִָֽם׃

passages.text: And he did evil in the sight of the LORD by following the abominations of the nations that the LORD had driven out before the Israelites.
passages.sermon:
Manasseh was king in Jerusalem.
Manasseh did evil.
The LORD saw Manasseh’s evil actions.
Manasseh followed the abominations of the nations.
The LORD had driven out those nations before the Israelites.
passages.original: וַיַּ֥עַשׂ הָרַ֖ע בְּעֵינֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה כְּתֽוֹעֲבוֹת֙ הַגּוֹיִ֔ם אֲשֶׁר֙ הוֹרִ֣ישׁ יְהוָ֔ה מִפְּנֵ֖י בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

passages.text: For he rebuilt the high places that his father Hezekiah had torn down, and he raised up altars for the Baals and made Asherah poles. And he worshiped and served all the host of heaven.
passages.sermon:
Manasseh was king in Jerusalem.
Hezekiah was his father.
Hezekiah had torn down the high places.
Manasseh rebuilt those high places.
Manasseh set up altars for the Baals.
He made Asherah poles.
Manasseh worshiped all the host of heaven.
He served them.
passages.original: וַיָּ֗שָׁב וַיִּ֙בֶן֙ אֶת־ הַבָּמ֔וֹת אֲשֶׁ֥ר נִתַּ֖ץ יְחִזְקִיָּ֣הוּ אָבִ֑יו וַיָּ֨קֶם מִזְבְּח֤וֹת לַבְּעָלִים֙ וַיַּ֣עַשׂ אֲשֵׁר֔וֹת וַיִּשְׁתַּ֙חוּ֙ לְכָל־ צְבָ֣א הַשָּׁמַ֔יִם וַֽיַּעֲבֹ֖ד אֹתָֽם׃

passages.text: Manasseh also built altars in the house of the LORD, of which the LORD had said, “My Name will remain in Jerusalem forever.”
passages.sermon:
Manasseh was king of Judah.
Manasseh built altars inside the house of the LORD.
The house of the LORD was the temple in Jerusalem.
The LORD had said, “My Name will remain in Jerusalem forever.”
Manasseh built these altars in the very place where God had chosen to put His Name forever.
passages.original: וּבָנָ֥ה מִזְבְּח֖וֹת בְּבֵ֣ית יְהוָ֑ה אֲשֶׁר֙ אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה בִּירוּשָׁלִַ֥ם יִֽהְיֶה־ שְּׁמִ֖י לְעוֹלָֽם׃

passages.text: In both courtyards of the house of the LORD, he built altars to all the host of heaven.
passages.sermon:
Manasseh was king of Judah.
He did evil in the sight of the LORD.
He built altars in both courtyards of the house of the LORD.
He built these altars for all the host of heaven.
The house of the LORD was in Jerusalem.
The host of heaven means the sun, moon, and stars.
God had said His Name would be in Jerusalem forever.
passages.original: וַיִּ֥בֶן מִזְבְּח֖וֹת לְכָל־ צְבָ֣א הַשָּׁמָ֑יִם בִּשְׁתֵּ֖י חַצְר֥וֹת בֵּית־ יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: He sacrificed his sons in the fire in the Valley of Hinnom. He practiced sorcery, divination, and witchcraft, and consulted mediums and spiritists. He did great evil in the sight of the LORD, provoking Him to anger.
passages.sermon:
Manasseh was king of Judah.
Manasseh sacrificed his sons in the fire.
He did this in the Valley of Hinnom.
Manasseh practiced sorcery.
He practiced divination.
He practiced witchcraft.
He consulted mediums.
He consulted spiritists.
Manasseh did great evil in the sight of the LORD.
He provoked the LORD to anger.
passages.original: וְהוּא֩ הֶעֱבִ֨יר אֶת־ בָּנָ֤יו בָּאֵשׁ֙ בְּגֵ֣י בֶן־ הִנֹּ֔ם וְעוֹנֵ֤ן וְנִחֵשׁ֙ וְֽכִשֵּׁ֔ף וְעָ֥שָׂה א֖וֹב וְיִדְּעוֹנִ֑י הִרְבָּ֗ה לַעֲשׂ֥וֹת הָרַ֛ע בְּעֵינֵ֥י יְהוָ֖ה לְהַכְעִיסֽוֹ׃

passages.text: Manasseh even took the carved image he had made and set it up in the house of God, of which God had said to David and his son Solomon, “In this temple and in Jerusalem, which I have chosen out of all the tribes of Israel, I will establish My Name forever.
passages.sermon:
Manasseh was king of Judah.
Manasseh made a carved image.
Manasseh took the carved image.
Manasseh set the carved image in the house of God.
The house of God is the temple in Jerusalem.
God spoke to David and to Solomon, David’s son.
God said He chose this temple and Jerusalem from all the tribes of Israel.
God said He would put His Name in this temple and in Jerusalem forever.
passages.original: וַיָּ֕שֶׂם אֶת־ פֶּ֥סֶל הַסֶּ֖מֶל אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשָׂ֑ה בְּבֵ֣ית הָאֱלֹהִ֗ים אֲשֶׁ֨ר אָמַ֤ר אֱלֹהִים֙ אֶל־ דָּוִיד֙ וְאֶל־ שְׁלֹמֹ֣ה בְנ֔וֹ בַּבַּ֨יִת הַזֶּ֜ה וּבִֽירוּשָׁלִַ֗ם אֲשֶׁ֤ר בָּחַ֙רְתִּי֙ מִכֹּל֙ שִׁבְטֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אָשִׂ֥ים אֶת־ שְׁמִ֖י לְעֵילֽוֹם׃

passages.text: I will never again cause the feet of the Israelites to leave the land that I assigned to your fathers, if only they are careful to do all that I have commanded them through Moses—all the laws, statutes, and judgments.”
passages.sermon:
God spoke to the people of Israel.
God promised not to remove the Israelites from their land again.
God had given this land to their ancestors.
God required the Israelites to obey Him.
They must carefully do everything He commanded them.
God gave these commands through Moses.
These commands include all the laws, statutes, and judgments.
passages.original: וְלֹ֣א אוֹסִ֗יף לְהָסִיר֙ אֶת־ רֶ֣גֶל יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל מֵעַל֙ הָֽאֲדָמָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר הֶֽעֱמַ֖דְתִּי לַאֲבֹֽתֵיכֶ֑ם רַ֣ק׀ אִם־ יִשְׁמְר֣וּ לַעֲשׂ֗וֹת אֵ֚ת כָּל־ אֲשֶׁ֣ר צִוִּיתִ֔ים לְכָל־ הַתּוֹרָ֛ה וְהַֽחֻקִּ֥ים וְהַמִּשְׁפָּטִ֖ים בְּיַד־ מֹשֶֽׁה׃

passages.text: So Manasseh led the people of Judah and Jerusalem astray, so that they did greater evil than the nations that the LORD had destroyed before the Israelites.
passages.sermon:
Manasseh was king of Judah.
He led the people of Judah astray.
He also led the people of Jerusalem astray.
He caused them to do evil things.
They did more evil than the nations.
The LORD had destroyed those nations before the Israelites.
The people of Judah and Jerusalem became worse than those nations.
passages.original: וַיֶּ֣תַע מְנַשֶּׁ֔ה אֶת־ יְהוּדָ֖ה וְיֹשְׁבֵ֣י יְרוּשָׁלִָ֑ם לַעֲשׂ֣וֹת רָ֔ע מִן־ הַ֨גּוֹיִ֔ם אֲשֶׁר֙ הִשְׁמִ֣יד יְהוָ֔ה מִפְּנֵ֖י בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃פ

passages.text: And the LORD spoke to Manasseh and his people, but they did not listen.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is the God of Israel.
The LORD spoke to Manasseh.
The LORD spoke to Manasseh’s people.
Manasseh did not listen to the LORD.
Manasseh’s people did not listen to the LORD.
passages.original: וַיְדַבֵּ֧ר יְהוָ֛ה אֶל־ מְנַשֶּׁ֥ה וְאֶל־ עַמּ֖וֹ וְלֹ֥א הִקְשִֽׁיבוּ׃

passages.text: So the LORD brought against them the military commanders of the king of Assyria, who captured Manasseh, put a hook in his nose, bound him with bronze shackles, and took him to Babylon.
passages.sermon:
The LORD acted against Manasseh and his people.
The LORD sent the military commanders of the king of Assyria.
These commanders captured Manasseh.
They put a hook in Manasseh’s nose.
They bound Manasseh with bronze shackles.
They took Manasseh to Babylon.
passages.original: וַיָּבֵ֨א יְהוָ֜ה עֲלֵיהֶ֗ם אֶת־ שָׂרֵ֤י הַצָּבָא֙ אֲשֶׁר֙ לְמֶ֣לֶךְ אַשּׁ֔וּר וַיִּלְכְּד֥וּ אֶת־ מְנַשֶּׁ֖ה בַּחֹחִ֑ים וַיַּֽאַסְרֻ֙הוּ֙ בַּֽנְחֻשְׁתַּ֔יִם וַיּוֹלִיכֻ֖הוּ בָּבֶֽלָה׃

passages.text: And in his distress, Manasseh sought the favor of the LORD his God and earnestly humbled himself before the God of his fathers.
passages.sermon:
Manasseh was king of Judah.
Manasseh did evil and did not listen to God.
God allowed Manasseh to be captured and taken to Babylon.
Manasseh became very distressed.
Manasseh sought help from the LORD his God.
Manasseh prayed to God.
Manasseh humbled himself greatly before the God of his ancestors.
passages.original: וּכְהָצֵ֣ר ל֔וֹ חִלָּ֕ה אֶת־ פְּנֵ֖י יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהָ֑יו וַיִּכָּנַ֣ע מְאֹ֔ד מִלִּפְנֵ֖י אֱלֹהֵ֥י אֲבֹתָֽיו׃

passages.text: And when he prayed to Him, the LORD received his plea and heard his petition; so He brought him back to Jerusalem and to his kingdom. Then Manasseh knew that the LORD is God.
passages.sermon:
Manasseh was king of Judah.
Manasseh prayed to the LORD.
The LORD listened to Manasseh’s prayer.
The LORD accepted Manasseh’s plea.
The LORD brought Manasseh back to Jerusalem.
The LORD restored Manasseh to his kingdom.
Manasseh understood that the LORD is God.
passages.original: וַיִּתְפַּלֵּ֣ל אֵלָ֗יו וַיֵּעָ֤תֶר לוֹ֙ וַיִּשְׁמַ֣ע תְּחִנָּת֔וֹ וַיְשִׁיבֵ֥הוּ יְרוּשָׁלִַ֖ם לְמַלְכוּת֑וֹ וַיֵּ֣דַע מְנַשֶּׁ֔ה כִּ֥י יְהוָ֖ה ה֥וּא הָֽאֱלֹהִֽים׃

passages.text: After this, Manasseh rebuilt the outer wall of the City of David from west of Gihon in the valley to the entrance of the Fish Gate, and he brought it around the hill of Ophel and heightened it considerably. He also stationed military commanders in all the fortified cities of Judah.
passages.sermon:
Manasseh was king of Judah.
After these events, Manasseh rebuilt the outer wall of the City of David.
He started at the west side of Gihon in the valley.
He continued to the entrance of the Fish Gate.
He brought the wall around the hill of Ophel.
He made the wall much higher.
Manasseh placed military commanders in every fortified city in Judah.
passages.original: וְאַחֲרֵי־ כֵ֡ן בָּנָ֣ה חוֹמָ֣ה חִֽיצוֹנָ֣ה׀ לְעִיר־ דָּוִ֡יד מַעְרָבָה֩ לְגִיח֨וֹן בַּנַּ֜חַל וְלָב֨וֹא בְשַׁ֤עַר הַדָּגִים֙ וְסָבַ֣ב לָעֹ֔פֶל וַיַּגְבִּיהֶ֖הָ מְאֹ֑ד וַיָּ֧שֶׂם שָֽׂרֵי־ חַ֛יִל בְּכָל־ הֶעָרִ֥ים הַבְּצֻר֖וֹת בִּיהוּדָֽה׃

passages.text: He removed the foreign gods and the idol from the house of the LORD, along with all the altars he had built on the temple mount and in Jerusalem, and he dumped them outside the city.
passages.sermon:
Manasseh was king of Judah.
Manasseh had built altars to foreign gods.
Manasseh had placed idols in the house of the LORD.
Manasseh removed the foreign gods from the house of the LORD.
Manasseh took the idol out of the house of the LORD.
Manasseh removed all the altars he had built on the temple mount.
Manasseh removed all the altars he had built in Jerusalem.
Manasseh threw all these things outside the city.
passages.original: וַ֠יָּסַר אֶת־ אֱלֹהֵ֨י הַנֵּכָ֤ר וְאֶת־ הַסֶּ֙מֶל֙ מִבֵּ֣ית יְהוָ֔ה וְכָל־ הַֽמִּזְבְּח֗וֹת אֲשֶׁ֥ר בָּנָ֛ה בְּהַ֥ר בֵּית־ יְהוָ֖ה וּבִירוּשָׁלִָ֑ם וַיַּשְׁלֵ֖ךְ ח֥וּצָה לָעִֽיר׃

passages.text: Then he restored the altar of the LORD and sacrificed peace offerings and thank offerings on it, and he told Judah to serve the LORD, the God of Israel.
passages.sermon:
Manasseh was king of Judah.
He restored the altar of the LORD.
He offered peace offerings on the altar.
He offered thank offerings on the altar.
He told the people of Judah to serve the LORD.
The LORD is the God of Israel.
passages.original: וַיָּכֶן אֶת־ מִזְבַּ֣ח יְהוָ֔ה וַיִּזְבַּ֣ח עָלָ֔יו זִבְחֵ֥י שְׁלָמִ֖ים וְתוֹדָ֑ה וַיֹּ֙אמֶר֙ לִֽיהוּדָ֔ה לַעֲב֕וֹד אֶת־ יְהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

passages.text: Nevertheless, the people still sacrificed at the high places, but only to the LORD their God.
passages.sermon:
The people of Judah still offered sacrifices.
They sacrificed at the high places.
They did not worship other gods there.
They sacrificed only to the LORD.
The LORD was their God.
passages.original: אֲבָל֙ ע֣וֹד הָעָ֔ם זֹבְחִ֖ים בַּבָּמ֑וֹת רַ֖ק לַיהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵיהֶֽם׃

passages.text: As for the rest of the acts of Manasseh, along with his prayer to his God and the words of the seers who spoke to him in the name of the LORD, the God of Israel, they are indeed written in the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel.
passages.sermon:
Manasseh was a king of Judah.
He did many things during his reign.
He prayed to his God.
Seers spoke to Manasseh.
These seers spoke in the name of the LORD, the God of Israel.
The rest of Manasseh’s deeds are written down.
His prayer is also written down.
The words of the seers are written down too.
All these things are recorded in the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel.
passages.original: וְיֶ֨תֶר דִּבְרֵ֣י מְנַשֶּׁה֮ וּתְפִלָּת֣וֹ אֶל־ אֱלֹהָיו֒ וְדִבְרֵי֙ הַֽחֹזִ֔ים הַֽמְדַבְּרִ֣ים אֵלָ֔יו בְּשֵׁ֥ם יְהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל הִנָּ֕ם עַל־ דִּבְרֵ֖י מַלְכֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

passages.text: His prayer and how God received his plea, as well as all his sin and unfaithfulness, and the sites where he built high places and set up Asherah poles and idols before he humbled himself, they are indeed written in the Records of the Seers.
passages.sermon:
Manasseh was king of Judah.
He prayed to God.
God listened to Manasseh’s plea.
Manasseh sinned against God.
Manasseh was unfaithful to God.
He built high places for worship.
He set up Asherah poles.
He made idols.
He did these things before he humbled himself before God.
The records of the seers contain these events.
The records include his prayer, God’s response, his sins, his unfaithfulness, and the places he built for false worship.
passages.original: וּתְפִלָּת֣וֹ וְהֵֽעָתֶר־ לוֹ֮ וְכָל־ חַטָּאת֣וֹ וּמַעְלוֹ֒ וְהַמְּקֹמ֗וֹת אֲשֶׁר֩ בָּנָ֨ה בָהֶ֤ם בָּמוֹת֙ וְהֶעֱמִיד֙ הָאֲשֵׁרִ֣ים וְהַפְּסִלִ֔ים לִפְנֵ֖י הִכָּנְע֑וֹ הִנָּ֣ם כְּתוּבִ֔ים עַ֖ל דִּבְרֵ֥י חוֹזָֽי׃

passages.text: And Manasseh rested with his fathers and was buried at his palace. And his son Amon reigned in his place.
passages.sermon:
Manasseh was king of Judah.
Manasseh died.
People buried Manasseh in his palace.
Amon was Manasseh’s son.
Amon became king after Manasseh.
passages.original: וַיִּשְׁכַּ֤ב מְנַשֶּׁה֙ עִם־ אֲבֹתָ֔יו וַֽיִּקְבְּרֻ֖הוּ בֵּית֑וֹ וַיִּמְלֹ֛ךְ אָמ֥וֹן בְּנ֖וֹ תַּחְתָּֽיו׃פ

passages.text: Amon was twenty-two years old when he became king, and he reigned in Jerusalem two years.
passages.sermon: Amon became king when he was twenty-two years old.\r\nAmon ruled in Jerusalem.\r\nAmon reigned for two years.
passages.original: בֶּן־ עֶשְׂרִ֧ים וּשְׁתַּ֛יִם שָׁנָ֖ה אָמ֣וֹן בְּמָלְכ֑וֹ וּשְׁתַּ֣יִם שָׁנִ֔ים מָלַ֖ךְ בִּֽירוּשָׁלִָֽם׃

passages.text: And he did evil in the sight of the LORD, as his father Manasseh had done. Amon served and sacrificed to all the idols that his father Manasseh had made, but he did not humble himself before the LORD as his father Manasseh had done; instead, Amon increased his guilt.
passages.sermon:
Amon was king in Jerusalem.
Amon did evil in the sight of the LORD.
Amon acted like his father Manasseh.
Manasseh was also evil.
Manasseh made many idols.
Amon served these idols.
Amon sacrificed to these idols.
Amon did not humble himself before the LORD.
Manasseh had humbled himself before the LORD.
Amon did not follow his father’s example in this.
Amon increased his guilt before God.
passages.original: וַיַּ֤עַשׂ הָרַע֙ בְּעֵינֵ֣י יְהוָ֔ה כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשָׂ֖ה מְנַשֶּׁ֣ה אָבִ֑יו וּֽלְכָל־ הַפְּסִילִ֗ים אֲשֶׁ֤ר עָשָׂה֙ מְנַשֶּׁ֣ה אָבִ֔יו זִבַּ֥ח אָמ֖וֹן וַיַּֽעַבְדֵֽם׃ וְלֹ֤א נִכְנַע֙ מִלִּפְנֵ֣י יְהוָ֔ה כְּהִכָּנַ֖ע מְנַשֶּׁ֣ה אָבִ֑יו כִּ֛י ה֥וּא אָמ֖וֹן הִרְבָּ֥ה אַשְׁמָֽה׃

passages.text: Then the servants of Amon conspired against him and killed him in his palace.
passages.sermon: Amon was king in Jerusalem.\r\nHis servants made a secret plan against him.\r\nThey killed Amon in his own palace.
passages.original: וַיִּקְשְׁר֤וּ עָלָיו֙ עֲבָדָ֔יו וַיְמִיתֻ֖הוּ בְּבֵיתֽוֹ׃

passages.text: But the people of the land killed all those who had conspired against King Amon, and they made his son Josiah king in his place.
passages.sermon:
The people of the land acted together.
They killed everyone who had conspired against King Amon.
King Amon was Josiah’s father.
The people of the land made Josiah king after Amon died.
Josiah became king in his father’s place.
passages.original: וַיַּכּוּ֙ עַם־ הָאָ֔רֶץ אֵ֥ת כָּל־ הַקֹּֽשְׁרִ֖ים עַל־ הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ אָמ֑וֹן וַיַּמְלִ֧יכוּ עַם־ הָאָ֛רֶץ אֶת־ יֹאשִׁיָּ֥הוּ בְנ֖וֹ תַּחְתָּֽיו׃פ
